newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - ScotPower sees benefits of buy.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - ScotPower sees benefits of buy.

text.p: British multi-utility Scottish Power Plc expects both customers and shareholders to benefit from the integration of Southern Water which it bought for 1.68 billion stg in August, chief executive Ian Robinson said.
"We would expect to improve customer services...Scottish Power shareholders will strongly benefit as well," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Robinson pointed out that savings from integration of the water and sewerage company were above expectations, giving a 52 million stg a year boost to pretax profits, while reorganisation costs of 21.2 million stg were lower than envisaged.
"We are very pleased with what we have found...we are now focusing back on the core business," Robinson said.

He added that around 200 to 300 jobs could be created over a couple of years as ScotPower expands its retail business and positions itself to compete in gas and electricity markets when these are liberalised in 1998.
ScotPower said in a statement that a total 2,050 jobs would go as a result of the acquisition of Southern Water but Robinson said 580 of these would be voluntary redundancies.

He said planned disposals totalling 100 million stg would include 70 million stg of business sales including vehicle leasing interests, water bottling and landfill waste sites along with 30 million stg from property.
Looking ahead to liberalisation of electricity and gas supply markets in 1998, Robinson said the company was well positioned.
"All our businesses are strongly competitive...we are focused on five million customers (to offer) a broader range, good customer services and competitive rates," he said.
ScotPower, which bought regional electricity company (Rec) Manweb last year, said half-year pre-tax profits after restructuring costs rose to 167 million stg from 127.7 million stg a year ago.
It paid out an interim dividend of 6.17 pence, up from 5.17 pence and said the final dividend for the year would be 18.5 pence, up 19 percent.
